chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Abi Zahir, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Yusuf al-Abzari, from al-Mufaddal, who said:
Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام said to me one day—and before that he had not addressed me by my kunyah—: “O Abu ‘Abdillah.”

He said: I said, “At your service.” He said: “For us, in every Friday night, there is joy.” I said: “May Allah increase you, and what is that?” He said: “When it is Friday night, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله reaches the Throne, and the Imams عليهم السلام reach it with him, and we reach it with them. So our spirits are not returned to our bodies except with acquired knowledge, and were it not for that, we would be exhausted.”

key_terms.أَرْوَاحُنَا: our spirits, referring to their souls returning to their bodies
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: the Imams عليهم السلام, who accompany the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.الْعَرْشَ: the Throne, indicating an exalted station of divine proximity
key_terms.سُرُورًا: joy or delight experienced on that night
key_terms.عِلْمٍ مُسْتَفَادٍ: acquired or newly bestowed knowledge gained through that encounter
key_terms.لَأَنْفَدْنَا: we would be exhausted or depleted without that replenishment
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ الْجُمُعَةِ: the night of Friday, presented here as a recurring time of special grace

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the increase of the Imams’ knowledge on Friday night?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a special distinction of Friday night for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and the Imams عليهم السلام, during which they attain nearness to the Throne. It presents their return as accompanied by newly acquired knowledge, indicating a continual divine increase granted to them.
